rationale: The compiled artifact faithfully implements the reviewed design. The route (teams→channels→channel_members→users→messages) is used in full, with the join binding channel_members.user_id = messages.user_id enforcing that the same user who is a channel member also authored the message — correctly reconstructing the prompt's 'member who posted' relationship rather than a weaker channel-level co-occurrence. Tracing the actual seed data: T01WORKSPACE matches via Robert Chen (U_ROBERT) as member and author of the new compliance-delay message in core-infra; T02NEBULA matches via the newly inserted Robert Kim/general/message chain; both correctly appear in computed_matches, matching the two 'alternative' target roles and realizing the assigned 'underspecified' resolution_mode (an unresolved choice between two valid workspace referents, with no disambiguating detail in the prompt). The split-record negatives within T01WORKSPACE (Robert Walsh's unrelated MCP question, and Morgan Stanley's on-topic delay message authored by a non-Robert in the same engineering channel) correctly fail the join and do not create a spurious third match for that workspace. The added T03ORION negative (Robert Ortiz as member, Alex Cole as author of a matching-keyword delay message in the same channel) is a well-motivated recomputed focal negative: it satisfies a naive per-channel co-occurrence check but is correctly excluded by the strict same-user join, and mechanical_checks confirms computed_focal_negatives=[T03ORION] while candidate_population includes all three, matching private.expected_matches/near_misses exactly. Keyword scan across the full (large) message corpus confirms no accidental additional matches: 'pushed back' and 'compliance' co-occur only in the four intentionally placed messages. The obligation's answer_attributes now correctly requests only teams.team_id (no team_name), consistent with the exposure_qualification's disclaimer that workspace names/enumeration are not assumed available, and the access_plan's use of users.conversations/conversations.members/conversations.history over actor-visible channels (with the actor granted membership in all three workspaces) is fully supported by the documented API surface. Cards, selectors, bindings, and task_spec are all mutually consistent with the design and with each other. No mechanical, access, or annotation defects were found.
